seo.title: Homeless help in Glasgow - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Glasgow: emergency housing, outreach, meals, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

page.heading: Glasgow homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance: 999 or 112 Nowhere safe to stay, Monday–Thursday 8:45am–4:45pm; Friday to 3:55pm: Glasgow City Council 0141 287 0555 Nowhere safe outside those hours: council emergency service 0800 838 502 Sleeping outside or worried about someone on the street: Simon Community Scotland 0800 027 7466, free, 24 hours Urgent medical or mental-health help that is not life-threatening: NHS 111; choose the mental-health option when relevant
page.notice: Beds, meals, opening times and eligibility can change. Call before travelling when possible. A homeless application, outreach contact or referral does not guarantee a particular placement. Never pay someone who claims they can secure a council or charity bed.
page.intro:
Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you normally sleep and whether children, pregnancy, illness, disability, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or an animal affect what is safe. Contact the council even when you have no identification, no local connection or no phone credit.
Start here: if you have nowhere safe tonight, ask Glasgow City Council to take a homeless application and say that you need temporary accommodation. If you are outside, also call the Street Team. If the council refuses to take an application or provide a written decision, call Shelter Scotland urgently.
page.footer: Is something wrong or outdated? Submit a correction. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md

entries.title: Emergency services
entries.description:
Phone: 999 or 112.
Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another threat to life. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first.
NHS Scotland emergency guidance

entries.title: Glasgow City Council: homeless application
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 287 0555, Monday–Thursday 8:45am–4:45pm and Friday 8:45am–3:55pm. Out of hours: 0800 838 502.
Say: “I am homeless and want to make a homeless application. I need temporary accommodation tonight.” In Scotland, the council must take an application and provide temporary accommodation when it has reason to believe you may be homeless and need it while the case is assessed.
Shelter Scotland: Glasgow council route and rights | Scottish Government homelessness guidance — https://scotland.shelter.org.uk/housing_advice/homeless/council_contact/glasgow

entries.title: In-person council homelessness teams
entries.description:
- South: Rowan Park, 5 Ardlaw Street, Glasgow G51 3RR.
- North East: 1250 Westerhouse Road, Glasgow G34 9EA.
- North West: 30 Mansion Street, Glasgow G22 5SZ.
- Asylum and Refugee service: 44 South Portland Street, Glasgow G5 9JJ.
Phone first when possible. Take any eviction letter, ID, benefit information or evidence of risk that you have, but missing papers should not stop you asking for help.
Addresses and application process

entries.title: Simon Community Scotland Street Team
entries.description:
Free helpline: 0800 027 7466, 24 hours.
The Glasgow Street Team works seven days a week with people sleeping outside. Give a precise public location, time and description. Outreach can offer practical support and connect someone to services, but it cannot promise a bed.
Street Team information

entries.title: Shelter Scotland housing helpline
entries.description:
Free phone: 0808 800 4444, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm.
Use it if the council will not accept an application, refuses temporary accommodation, offers somewhere unsafe or unsuitable, or you face eviction. Ask the council for every decision in writing. Shelter's Glasgow office is not a walk-in service.
Shelter Scotland contact options

entries.title: Severe weather and immediate safety
entries.description:
During extreme cold or other severe weather, call the council and Street Team for the current response. Arrangements and locations can change daily. Do not wait for a weather scheme if you are homeless: make a council application at any time of year.
Glasgow homelessness information

categories.title: Access hubs, day services and shelter pathways

entries.title: Simon Community Glasgow Access Hub
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 552 4164. Walk in without an appointment, usually Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 9am–5pm; Wednesday 10am–5pm.
Housing, benefits, health, finances, legal and digital support, with visiting services such as dental checks, haircuts, harm reduction and veterinary help. Ask on arrival which partners are present that day.
Simon Community access hubs
entries.address: Address: 74–80 Brown Street, Glasgow G2 8PD

entries.title: Glasgow City Mission: City Centre Project
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 221 2630. Weekday assistance sessions and an evening drop-in provide practical help, advocacy, food and routes into other services. The published programme changes, so check the current timetable.
The Mission is a Christian charity. Services support people regardless of belief; some optional groups have a religious focus.
Current City Centre Project timetable
entries.address: Address: 20 Crimea Street, Glasgow G2 8PW

entries.title: Lodging House Mission
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 552 0285; email: enquiries@lhm-glasgow.org.uk. Usually open Monday–Thursday 8:30am–3pm and Friday 8:30am–2pm. — mailto:enquiries@lhm-glasgow.org.uk
Day support, food, advice, activities and practical help for people who are homeless, vulnerable or socially excluded. It has a Christian ethos and provides help without judgement. Confirm the day's services before travelling.
Lodging House Mission
entries.address: Address: 35 East Campbell Street, Glasgow G1 5DT

entries.title: The Wayside Club Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 221 0169. Open every evening 6:45pm–8:30pm; also Saturday afternoon. Its Saturday pages publish slightly different afternoon times, so call before setting out.
Free food, showers, emergency clothes, sleeping bags, a small library, listening and advice. It is run by the Catholic Legion of Mary with helpers of other or no faith; Sunday Mass is optional.
Wayside services and current opening times
entries.address: Address: 32 Midland Street, Glasgow G1 4PR

entries.title: Homeless Project Scotland
entries.description:
Phone: 0800 999 2477. Its volunteer emergency shelter and soup kitchen operate subject to staffing, eligibility and capacity. Call for today's location and access before travelling.
The council should be contacted first for accommodation. A charity assessment does not guarantee a bed, and old online listings may not reflect that night's arrangements.
Night-shelter access rules | contact information — https://homelessprojectscotland.org/contact-us
entries.address: Contact address: 67 Glassford Street, Glasgow G1 1UL

entries.title: Glasgow City Mission Overnight Welcome Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 07513 567671.
This is seasonal emergency provision, not a year-round walk-in shelter. Contact the council first, then call the Mission to check whether the centre is operating, who can be referred and whether any place remains.
Current get-help and seasonal information

entries.title: Council temporary-accommodation casework
entries.description:
If the council has already placed you, use the team for your area: Asylum and Refugee 0141 222 7300; North West 0141 276 6168; North East 0141 276 6153; South 0141 276 8201; Prison Casework 0141 770 2123.
These numbers are for people already linked to temporary-accommodation casework. For a new homeless application use 0141 287 0555.
Published Glasgow support contacts

entries.title: If no charity bed is available
entries.description:
Return to the council and repeat that you need temporary accommodation. Ask for the decision and reasons in writing, the address of any alternative and safe travel instructions. Call Shelter Scotland or a housing solicitor quickly because review and court time limits can be short.
Shelter Scotland: temporary accommodation rights

entries.title: Glasgow City Mission evening dinner
entries.description:
The current weekday Evening Drop-In lists dinner from 6:30pm–8pm. Press buzzer 0. Check the live timetable because holiday and programme changes occur.
City Centre Project timetable
entries.address: Address: 20 Crimea Street, Glasgow G2 8PW

entries.title: Lodging House Mission breakfast and lunch
entries.description:
The service publishes weekday food support, including breakfast and a free lunch. The provider's current opening time is 8:30am; third-party meal timetables differ, so call 0141 552 0285 to confirm before travelling.
Lodging House Mission | Glasgow Helps food listing — https://www.glasgowhelps.org/services/food-service-at-lodging-house-mission
entries.address: Address: 35 East Campbell Street, Glasgow G1 5DT

entries.title: The Wayside Club: free evening food
entries.description:
Free soup, sandwiches, tea, coffee and take-away sandwiches every evening 6:45pm–8:30pm, including weekends and public holidays. Emergency food parcels may also be available.
Wayside food and opening times
entries.address: Address: 32 Midland Street, Glasgow G1 4PR

entries.title: Homeless Project Scotland soup kitchen
entries.description:
The charity publishes an evening soup-kitchen programme operated by volunteers. The public serving point can change: call 0800 999 2477 for today's verified location and time rather than relying on an old map.
Soup-kitchen programme

entries.title: Glasgow Central Mosque food parcels
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 429 3132. The mosque publishes a Sunday poverty-relief food-parcel session, normally 1pm–3pm. Support is available regardless of faith; call to confirm stock and the current collection process.
Glasgow Central Mosque poverty relief
entries.address: Address: 1 Mosque Avenue, Glasgow G5 9TA

entries.title: Shri Guru Tegh Bahadur Gurdwara: langar
entries.description:
The Sikh community shares free langar with anyone, regardless of religion, gender, ethnicity or income, especially around the Sunday congregation. Cover your head, remove shoes, dress conservatively and take no tobacco, alcohol or intoxicants onto the premises. Confirm serving time before travel.
Gurdwara welcome and langar information
entries.address: Address: 32 St Andrew's Drive, Glasgow

entries.title: Find a local foodbank or community meal
entries.description:
Glasgow Helps and the Independent Food Aid Network list community food organisations. Some need a voucher, postcode, appointment or referral; others offer open meals. Contact the provider before travelling.
Glasgow Helps directory

entries.title: Glasgow City Mission showers and practical support
entries.description:
Showers and basic practical help are listed at the City Centre Project. Availability can depend on capacity; ask at reception and check the day's timetable.
City Centre Project

entries.title: The Wayside Club showers and emergency items
entries.description:
Showers for men and women, emergency clothes and sleeping bags are offered during opening sessions, subject to supplies. Call 0141 221 0169 if an item is urgent.
Wayside practical help

entries.title: Simon Community Access Hub
entries.description:
Ask about clothing, toiletries, haircuts and the current practical-support programme. Visiting services operate on set days and can fill up.
Access Hub

entries.title: Lodging House Mission practical help
entries.description:
Ask at reception about the current clothing, hygiene and laundry arrangements. Do not rely on an old directory entry: published activities and supplies change.
Lodging House Mission

entries.title: Bags and storage
entries.description:
No permanently available free public luggage-storage service was verified. Ask an access hub or caseworker before leaving anything; get a receipt and collection deadline. Never leave identification, medication or all belongings in an unattended bag.
Ask the Access Hub about current options

categories.title: Health, dental and sexual health care

entries.title: Immediate and urgent medical help
entries.description:
Call 999 or 112 for a life-threatening emergency. For urgent help that cannot wait but is not life-threatening, phone NHS 24 on 111. Calls are free.
When to phone 111 or 999

entries.title: Register with a GP without proof of address
entries.description:
Anyone in Scotland can use primary care without charge. A GP should not delay or refuse registration because you cannot provide identification or proof of address. If staying under three months, ask to be treated as a temporary resident.
Ask Simon Community or Glasgow City Mission for help finding a practice and completing the form.
NHS Scotland GP registration rights

entries.title: Pharmacy First Scotland
entries.description:
Community pharmacists can assess and treat many minor illnesses and provide NHS advice. Ask whether a consultation is free under NHS Pharmacy First Scotland and say if you have no GP.
Pharmacy First Scotland | find a pharmacy — https://www.nhsinform.scot/scotlands-service-directory/pharmacies/

entries.title: Glasgow Dental Hospital: urgent dental care
entries.description:
This is not a walk-in service. If you are not registered with a dentist, call 0141 232 6323 for daytime assessment. Outside service hours, call NHS 24 on 111. Severe swelling affecting breathing or swallowing is a 999 emergency.
Dental Hospital access information
entries.address: Address: 378 Sauchiehall Street, Glasgow G2 3JZ

entries.title: Sandyford sexual health
entries.description:
Appointments and advice: 0141 211 8130, Monday–Friday 8:45am–4pm. Appointment-only services include STI testing and treatment, contraception, PrEP and abortion care. When closed, use NHS 24 on 111; most pharmacies can provide emergency contraception.
NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde sexual-health guidance

entries.title: Archway sexual-assault response
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 211 8175. Archway is a 24-hour, appointment-only NHS service for people raped or sexually assaulted in the past seven days. You can seek health care without first reporting to police. In immediate danger call 999.
NHS sexual-assault service information

entries.title: Access Hub visiting health services
entries.description:
Simon Community lists visiting health professionals, dental checks, harm-reduction workers and veterinary support. Ask reception for the current weekly programme; a drop-in does not guarantee same-day treatment.
Access Hub support

entries.title: NHS 24 Mental Health Hub
entries.description:
Phone 111 and choose the mental-health option, 24 hours. If a life is at immediate risk, there has been a serious overdose or someone is badly injured, call 999.
NHS urgent mental-health help

entries.title: Breathing Space
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 83 85 87. Confidential support for anyone in Scotland aged 16+ feeling low, depressed or anxious; 6pm–2am on weekdays and 24 hours at weekends.
Breathing Space

entries.title: Samaritans
entries.description:
Free phone: 116 123, 24 hours, every day. You do not need to be suicidal and do not need phone credit. Samaritans listens but is not an emergency or accommodation service.
Contact Samaritans

entries.title: Link Up alcohol and drug crisis support
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 420 1929, 24 hours for advice and support. No professional referral is needed to ask for help. Residential crisis support requires assessment and is never guaranteed on first contact.
NHS alcohol and drug services
entries.address: Address: 112 Commerce Street, Tradeston, Glasgow G5 8DW

entries.title: Local alcohol and drug recovery services
entries.description:
NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde lists community recovery teams and a specialist homelessness service. Call Link Up or use the directory for the correct team; say if you are sleeping outside, withdrawing, pregnant or at overdose risk.
Find a recovery service

entries.title: Glasgow City Mission counselling
entries.description:
Self-referral phone: 07789 986657. The City Centre Project publishes appointment-based counselling, normally Wednesday–Friday during daytime hours. It is not a crisis line.
City Mission counselling and timetable

categories.title: Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

entries.title: The Mitchell Library
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 287 2999. Free entry, Wi-Fi, public computers, printing and accessible toilets. Normally open Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 9am–5pm; Tuesday and Thursday to 8pm; closed Sunday.
There is no public locker or cloakroom. Computer booking needs free library membership, but walk-up use may be possible.
Mitchell Library facilities and hours
entries.address: Address: North Street, Glasgow G3 7DN

entries.title: Glasgow libraries
entries.description:
Local libraries provide free Wi-Fi, computers and warm indoor space during their own hours. A free library card makes computer booking easier; ask staff what identity or address alternatives they can accept.
Find a Glasgow library | library computer and membership FAQ — https://www.glasgowlife.org.uk/libraries/frequently-asked-questions

entries.title: Access Hub and day services
entries.description:
Simon Community's hub and Glasgow City Mission can help with online forms, phone charging and digital access during their published sessions. Ask before plugging in equipment and keep devices in sight.
Simon Access Hub | City Mission timetable — https://www.glasgowcitymission.com/what-we-do/city-centre-projects/

entries.title: Public toilets
entries.description:
Use staffed libraries, day centres and transport stations during opening hours. Toilet access and charges can change, so ask staff. For an accessible toilet search, use the official Changing Places map.
Changing Places toilet map

entries.title: Plan a public-transport journey
entries.description:
Traveline Scotland provides live bus, rail, Subway and ferry planning. Check the last service and fare before travelling; overnight timetables are limited.
Traveline Scotland journey planner

entries.title: Glasgow Subway
entries.description:
Contactless, Smartcard and paper tickets are available; cash remains available at ticket offices or machines. Current fares and concessions can change. National Entitlement Card discounts on the Subway have local conditions and may not apply before 9am on weekdays.
SPT Subway tickets and current fares

entries.title: Free bus travel for eligible residents
entries.description:
People aged 5–21 who live in Scotland can travel free on most buses with a valid Young Scot or National Entitlement Card. Eligible people aged 60+ and disabled people can use the older/disabled scheme. A card is required; travel is not free while waiting for a replacement.
Under-22 scheme | 60+ and disabled scheme — https://www.transport.gov.scot/concessionary-travel/60plus-or-disabled-free-bus-travel/

entries.title: Ask about essential appointment travel
entries.description:
A housing, health, Jobcentre or charity worker may sometimes authorise a ticket for a specific appointment, but help is not automatic. Ask before buying a ticket, keep appointment evidence and never pay a stranger for an unofficial pass.
Ask at Simon Community Access Hub

entries.title: Glasgow Airport Express 500
entries.description:
The official 500 bus runs between Buchanan Bus Station stance 46 and Glasgow Airport stance 1, with service through the night and frequent daytime departures. Buy on board with cash, contactless or card, or online; check live disruptions and the fare first.
If stranded at the airport, speak to airport staff or police. The terminal is not accommodation; call the council out-of-hours number if you have nowhere safe.
Official Airport Express route and timetable

categories.title: Benefits, emergency money and housing costs

entries.title: Scottish Welfare Fund: Crisis Grant
entries.description:
A Crisis Grant may help with immediate short-term needs after an emergency or disaster when wellbeing is at serious risk. It is administered by Glasgow City Council and does not need to be repaid. Apply before spending money when possible.
Application help: 0141 276 1177, option 1, normally Monday–Friday 10am–4pm.
Apply through Glasgow City Council | 2026 Crisis Grant rules — https://www.gov.scot/publications/scottish-welfare-fund-statutory-guidance-2/pages/8/

entries.title: Scottish Welfare Fund: Community Care Grant
entries.description:
This can help eligible people establish or maintain a settled home, including after homelessness. It may cover essential household items, but awards depend on circumstances and budget. Apply to the council; it is not cash for a same-night hostel.
Scottish Welfare Fund overview

entries.title: Universal Credit without a fixed address
entries.description:
You can claim while sleeping rough, sofa surfing or in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted friend, hostel, day centre or local Jobcentre as a “care of” address. Help exists if you lack ID, a bank account, internet or email.
Official homeless claimant guidance | make a claim — https://www.gov.uk/universal-credit/how-to-claim

entries.title: Citizens Advice Scotland
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 028 1456 to reach a local bureau by postcode. Help to Claim Universal Credit: 0800 023 2581, Monday–Friday 8am–6pm. Advice is free and confidential.
Citizens Advice contact options

entries.title: Social Security Scotland
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 182 2222. Ask about Scottish Child Payment, disability, carer, funeral, heating and Job Start payments. Local advisers can arrange a community appointment and interpreters are available.
Social Security Scotland contact and local support

entries.title: Housing Benefit in temporary or supported accommodation
entries.description:
Some people in council temporary or specified supported accommodation claim Housing Benefit for rent instead of the Universal Credit housing element. Ask the accommodation provider or council benefits team which claim applies before submitting duplicate information.
Glasgow Housing Benefit

entries.title: Jobs & Business Glasgow
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 123 2898; text: 07393 753298; email: contact@jbg.org.uk. Free employment, training, CV, interview and employer support for eligible Glasgow residents aged 16+. — sms:+447393753298 — mailto:contact@jbg.org.uk
Jobs & Business Glasgow
entries.address: Head office: Ladywell Business Centre, 94 Duke Street, Glasgow G4 0UW

entries.title: Jobcentre Plus
entries.description:
Use the official finder for the correct office and appointment route. Tell the work coach if homelessness, health, lack of phone/data or travel makes claimant commitments difficult. Changes should be recorded in the Universal Credit journal.
Contact Jobcentre Plus

entries.title: Find a Job
entries.description:
The government service lists vacancies and is free. Never pay an employer or recruiter to obtain a job, and do not send bank credentials or original identity documents to an unverified contact.
Search official Find a Job vacancies

entries.title: Glasgow City Mission learning programme
entries.description:
The City Centre Project publishes computing, ESOL and other learning sessions. Some require registration and places can fill. Ask the Assistance team about current employment routes and access to a laptop.
Current programme

entries.title: Job Start Payment
entries.description:
Eligible young people who have been out of paid work and receive a qualifying benefit may get a Scottish payment towards starting a job. Check eligibility before assuming an award and apply within the deadline.
Job Start Payment

categories.title: Housing law, debt and legal advice

entries.title: Shelter Scotland
entries.description:
Free phone: 0808 800 4444, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Advice covers homeless applications, temporary accommodation, eviction, repairs and housing rights. The Glasgow office at 116 Osborne Street is not a public drop-in.
Shelter Scotland

entries.title: Govan Law Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 440 2503. Free, confidential legal services by appointment, including housing, homelessness, welfare benefits, debt, social services and consumer problems.
Govan Law Centre contact information
entries.address: Address: Units 4 and 6, 18–20 Orkney Street, Glasgow G51 2BZ

entries.title: Legal Services Agency
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 316 8450; office: 0141 353 3354. Housing solicitors can advise on homelessness decisions, temporary-accommodation suitability and court action. Contact them quickly because time limits apply.
Legal Services Agency
entries.address: Address: Savoy House, 2nd Floor, 140 Sauchiehall Street, Glasgow G2 3DH

entries.title: Citizens Advice: debt, benefits and consumer problems
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 028 1456. A local bureau can advise on debt, benefit decisions, utilities and employment. Ask creditors to pause action while advice is obtained, but do not ignore court papers or deadlines.
Find advice

entries.title: Police, hate crime and victim support
entries.description:
Call 999 for immediate danger; otherwise Police Scotland on 101. Victim Support Scotland provides free confidential support on 0800 160 1985. Reporting to a charity does not automatically make a police report.
Police Scotland contacts | Victim Support Scotland — https://www.scotland.police.uk/contact-us/

entries.title: Use a care-of address only with permission
entries.description:
Universal Credit can accept a hostel, trusted person, day centre or Jobcentre as a care-of address. Ask the organisation first, confirm the exact name and postcode, how often to collect mail and how long it will be held.
Official care-of address guidance

entries.title: Help with forms, email and identity checks
entries.description:
Simon Community Access Hub and Glasgow City Mission can help with online forms and digital access. Citizens Advice can help explain evidence requests. Never give a password, bank PIN or one-time security code to a helper.
Access Hub | Citizens Advice — https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/scotland/about-us/contact-us/

entries.title: Scottish birth, death, marriage or civil-partnership certificates
entries.description:
Order official replacement certificates from National Records of Scotland or a registrar, not an unofficial reseller. Fees apply; ask a caseworker whether a fund can help before ordering.
National Records of Scotland certificate ordering

entries.title: Lost or stolen British passport
entries.description:
Cancel a lost or stolen passport before replacing it. Costs and identity checks apply. HM Passport Office guidance recognises homelessness and lack of a postal address as vulnerabilities, so explain the situation and ask a charity or solicitor about a supporting letter.
Replace a lost or stolen passport | passport vulnerability guidance — https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/vulnerability-considerations-caseworker-guidance/vulnerability-considerations-for-passports-accessible

entries.title: Protect documents and accounts
entries.description:
Photograph important documents if safe, record reference numbers separately and report theft to the issuer. Do not store passwords with a phone or ID. Ask a service before using its address; unapproved mail may be returned.
UK cyber-security guidance

entries.title: Scottish Refugee Council
entries.description:
Free helpline: 0808 1967 274. Advice and appointments are arranged by helpline; there is no public drop-in. Support includes asylum, refugee integration, housing and destitution routes.
Scottish Refugee Council contact and opening information
entries.address: Office: Portland House, 17 Renfield Street, Glasgow G2 5AH

entries.title: Migrant Help asylum helpline
entries.description:
Free phone: 0808 8010 503, 24 hours. For people in the UK asylum system needing accommodation, financial support, reporting a problem or guidance. Accommodation is allocated through the asylum system and location cannot be promised.
Migrant Help asylum services

entries.title: Glasgow council asylum and refugee homelessness team
entries.description:
Use the council homelessness number 0141 287 0555. If already in the team's temporary accommodation, casework is on 0141 222 7300. Immigration eligibility can be complex: ask for written reasons and specialist advice.
Council homelessness route
entries.address: Address: 44 South Portland Street, Glasgow G5 9JJ

entries.title: Govan Community Project
entries.description:
Free helpline: 0800 310 0054, Monday–Thursday 10am–1pm. Advice and advocacy for refugees and people in the asylum system, with interpreter call-back where possible. There is a waiting list and the service cannot take every case.
Govan Community Project advice and current closures

entries.title: Positive Action in Housing
entries.description:
Homeless helpline: 0141 846 7179 during office hours; form help: 0141 353 2220. Housing, welfare, energy debt, eVisa and resettlement help for refugees, people seeking asylum and EU migrants. The main service is appointment-based; published outreach surgeries may be walk-in.
Current access and outreach details

entries.title: Human trafficking and modern slavery
entries.description:
Call 999 if someone is in immediate danger. The confidential Modern Slavery & Exploitation Helpline is 08000 121 700, 24 hours. Do not confront a suspected exploiter or arrange an unsafe escape alone.
Modern Slavery Helpline

entries.title: Scotland's Domestic Abuse and Forced Marriage Helpline
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 027 1234; text or WhatsApp: 07401 288595, 24 hours. Confidential help for anyone affected, with interpreters. In immediate danger call 999.
Domestic Abuse and Forced Marriage Helpline

entries.title: Glasgow Women's Aid
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 553 2022, normally Monday–Friday 9:30am–4:30pm. Support for women, children and young people affected by domestic abuse. Refuge access depends on assessment and space; refuge addresses are confidential.
Glasgow Women's Aid
entries.address: Office: 4th Floor, 30 Bell Street, Glasgow G1 1LG

entries.title: Simon Community Connect Hub for women
entries.description:
A women-only homelessness service offering housing, benefits, health, legal, advocacy, clothing and period products. The location is confidential for safety. Email: connecthub@simonscotland.org, or call the 24-hour Simon helpline on 0800 027 7466. — mailto:connecthub@simonscotland.org
Connect Hub

entries.title: Quarriers Stopover: ages 16–25
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 420 3121. Supported accommodation for young single people aged 16–25. Self-referral and referrals by others are accepted, but places are allocated by priority and availability.
Quarriers Stopover
entries.address: Address: 200 Pollokshaws Road, Glasgow G41 1QB

entries.title: Quarriers Youth Housing Support: ages 16–25
entries.description:
For single young people homeless or at risk who want housing in north or west Glasgow. Normally Monday–Friday 9am–7pm and Saturday 11am–7pm, with an on-call service outside those times. It provides prevention, tenancy and employment support, not a guaranteed walk-in bed.
Youth Housing Support Service
entries.address: Address: Maryhill Burgh Hall, Unit G3, 10–24 Gairbraid Avenue, 2nd Floor, Glasgow G20 8YE

entries.title: LGBT Health and Wellbeing helpline
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 464 7000, Tuesday–Thursday noon–9pm and Sunday 1pm–6pm. Emotional support and information on housing, benefits, hate crime, asylum and health for LGBTQ+ people across Scotland.
LGBT Helpline Scotland

entries.title: LGBT Health and Wellbeing Glasgow office
entries.description:
Phone: 0141 255 1767; email: glasgow@lgbthealth.org.uk. Contact ahead for the current programme; it is not an emergency shelter. — mailto:glasgow@lgbthealth.org.uk
Glasgow contact details
entries.address: Address: 14 North Claremont Street, Glasgow G3 7LE

entries.title: Military Matters: veterans and armed-forces families
entries.description:
Phone: 0131 510 1567. Housing Options Scotland offers free one-to-one housing advice for veterans, serving personnel, reservists, families and some bereaved or former partners. It is not a same-night accommodation service; use the council first in an emergency.
Military Matters

entries.title: Housing Options Scotland: disabled and older people
entries.description:
Free specialist housing advice for disabled people, older adults and veterans. The service may take several weeks to begin work, so use council homelessness services for tonight and submit the advice request for longer-term help.
Housing Options Scotland

entries.title: Age Scotland helpline
entries.description:
Free phone: 0800 12 44 222, Monday–Friday 9am–1pm. Information and friendship for older people, including benefits, housing and local services. This is not an emergency accommodation line.
Age Scotland helpline

entries.title: Simon Community Access Hub veterinary sessions
entries.description:
The Access Hub lists visiting veterinary support. Ask reception which day the vet attends, what animals can be seen and whether registration is needed. This is not a 24-hour animal emergency service.
Access Hub weekly services

entries.title: StreetVet
entries.description:
StreetVet offers free veterinary care to eligible pets belonging to people experiencing homelessness in supported locations. Complete the help form; coverage, registration and treatment depend on assessment. It does not provide general pet fostering or pay existing vet bills.
StreetVet help form

entries.title: Tell the council and shelter about your animal
entries.description:
Tell every referrer the species, size, health and vaccination status before travel. Some placements cannot accept animals and some may seek a pet-friendly option or temporary help. Never abandon a pet or assume an unconfirmed hostel will admit it.
Dogs Trust dog-friendly homelessness services
